text.p: H.F. Ahmanson & Co. , locked in a bitter takeover battle for rival California savings and loan Great Western Financial Corp., Tuesday reported higher-than-expected earnings.

The Irwindale, Calif.-based parent company of Home Savings of America said its net income rose 59 percent in the first quarter to $103.1 million, or 87 cents per share, from $64.8 million, or 45 cents.
The latest figure was far ahead of the 70 cents per share estimated by industry analysts.
"The earnings were a pleasant and positive surprise," said Thomas O'Donnell, analyst with Smith Barney.
"Ahmanson's doing all the right things and becoming more like a consumer bank," he said, citing improvements in credit quality and cost controls.
"This could help Ahmanson in its battle. It's not enough to turn the tide, but it's a positive step in that it's boosting the stock," he said.

Ahmanson initially launched a hostile bid in mid-February for Great Western and has been tenaciously fighting to complete the deal despite Great Western's rejection and its merger agreement, announced March 6, with white knight Washington Mutual Inc., which is based in Seattle.

Ahmanson's shares rose $1.625 to $37.125. Based on Tuesday's price, Ahmanson's bid to exchange up to 1.20 of its shares for each of Great Western's share was valued at $44.56 a share, or about $6.2 billion.
Rival Washington Mutual's offer to exchange 0.9 of its shares for each Great Western share also was valued at $6.2 billion Tuesday.
Ahmanson's results for that latest quarter included an after-tax gain of $9.5 million, or 8 cents per share on the sale of its Arizona branch system.
Net interest income totaled $317.6 million for the first quarter of 1997 vs. $317.0 million a year earlier.
In this year's quarter, non-interest income, excluding the gain on the sale of the Arizona branches, was $72.9 million, up from $60.5 million reported in the year-ago quarter.
Sanford Bernstein analyst Jonathan Gray raised his 1998 earnings forecast for Ahmanson to $3.40 a share from $3.30 a share after the thrift's first-quarter results exceeded his estimates.
Ahmanson has $48.7 billion in assets and operates 380 financial service centers in three states and 124 mortgage lending offices in eight states.
